key_insight: The paper finds that RL post-training does not need to update the entire transformer: training just a single layer can match the performance of full-parameter RL in some settings. This suggests RL gains are concentrated in specific layers rather than spread evenly across the model.
problem_solved: It addresses the assumption that all transformer layers contribute similarly during RL post-training, and asks whether full-model updates are actually necessary to achieve strong adaptation.
method: Perform a layer-wise study of RL training across transformer blocks instead of updating all parameters uniformly.
Compare performance when training individual layers or small subsets of layers against full-parameter RL training.
Analyze where RL adaptation is most effectively absorbed within the network.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could dramatically reduce RL training cost, memory use, and engineering complexity. It also offers a more targeted way to adapt LLMs during post-training without sacrificing performance.
visual_elements: Transformer stack diagram highlighting one trainable layer versus all layers frozen
Bar chart comparing performance of single-layer RL, few-layer RL, and full-parameter RL
Heatmap showing which layers change most during RL adaptation
Icon set for compute, memory, and accuracy trade-offs
paper_title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
paper_authors: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Athanasios Glentis, Dawei Li, Chung-Yiu Yau
